source.title: Understanding the Generalization Benefits of Late Learning Rate Decay
source.authors: Yinuo Ren; Chao Ma; Le-Xing Ying

record.file_problem: Full text is present; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures training and test loss while varying the timing of learning-rate decay for a VGG-11 on CIFAR-10, bearing on V1's training-error setting and V5's learning-rate scheduling behavior. It also analyzes a nonlinear regression model theoretically, but does not test the stated CIFAR classification or stability-threshold versions directly.
record.gate_note: Rows record the paper's own VGG-11 training-loss result and the reported training-loss landscape. Statements about prior work are not rows. No separate numerical training-loss values are given in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study investigates late learning-rate decay and generalization. Its VGG-11 experiment reports training loss, without specifying the classification loss or reporting training classification error, so it does not establish V1's named outcome. It does not measure learning rates relative to a stability threshold, curvature reduction, or threshold tracking required by V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The empirical experiment associates later learning-rate decay with lower final test loss. The theoretical explanation concerns a nonlinear reparameterized regression model analyzed in continuous time, with label-noise assumptions in Phase II; its effective dynamics approach the minimum-L2-norm training-loss solution. Near-optimal generalization requires additional assumptions, and discrete-time analysis remains future work.
record.recipe_differences: The experiment uses SGD and a delayed learning-rate reduction, but does not compare against a fixed, fully specified original claim recipe. The theoretical analysis is a nonlinear reparameterized regression model rather than a classification network.
record.method_sensitivity: For VGG-11 on CIFAR-10, the timing of learning-rate decay has little impact on subsequent training loss once stabilized, while later decay is associated with lower final testing loss.

fits_no_version.finding: VGG-11 training loss stabilizes after approximately 500 epochs; the projected landscape contains near-zero-loss minima, and decay timing has little effect on subsequent training loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD-trained VGG-11 on CIFAR-10 reaches a near-zero training-loss region under the reported learning-rate schedules.

fits_no_version.finding: Later decay from learning rate 0.1 to 0.01 yields lower final test loss in the VGG-11 experiment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Extending the large-learning-rate phase can improve final generalization after decay.

fits_no_version.finding: The nonlinear regression model's effective continuous-time dynamics approach a minimum-norm interpolating solution under the assumed noise and data conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noise-driven motion near a training-loss minima manifold can favor minimum-norm solutions before learning-rate decay.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS) 2024
record.problems: The empirical evidence shown here is one VGG-11 CIFAR-10 experiment; exact training-loss values and uncertainty estimates are not stated. The authors note that the loss-landscape visualization is only a 2D representation and may miss features of the full parameter space. Their analysis is predominantly continuous-time, with discrete-time analysis left for future work.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately reported numerical training-loss results appear in the supplied text. Results cited from other studies were excluded.

untested.parts: Training classification error from random initialization; size dependence, CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, Adam, and recipe comparisons.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training degradation with depth and comparisons involving identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Activation-matched initialization, signal propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and trainable depth.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, loss spikes with curvature reduction, divergence boundaries, and full-batch sharpness tracking.
Batch-normalization comparisons in training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both V1 verdicts. The reported loss does not establish the specified classification-error outcome, and untested datasets, architectures, and recipes do not justify limits_scope. The generalization and regression-theory findings do not test V5 merely because they involve large learning rates.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare model sizes, Adam, CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, smaller models, early stopping, or regularized recipes. The reported experiment varies learning-rate decay timing for VGG-11 on CIFAR-10.

rows.subject: VGG-11
rows.operation_detail: SGD training for 1000 epochs with initial learning rate 0.1; additional subpaths start at different main-path epochs and train for another 1000 epochs at learning rate 0.01.
rows.measure: Training loss over epochs; text says it stabilizes after the initial ∼500 epochs and describes the training-loss landscape as a near-zero-loss manifold.
rows.value: Training loss stabilizes after the initial ∼500 epochs; Figure 2a is described as a low-dimensional manifold of minima with near-zero training loss.
rows.note: The text does not give exact training-loss values. Timing of decay has a small impact on the subsequent training phase, according to the authors.
rows.check: The reported stabilization and near-zero training-loss landscape are accurate qualitative observations, but they do not directly establish near-zero training classification error. The classification loss, error rate, and initialization are unspecified. Stabilization alone also does not establish successful fitting. Retain as a training-loss finding without a V1 link.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports

reader_labels.reason: The authors report stabilized training loss and a near-zero training-loss minimum manifold; see R1. This supports the large-network training-error portion only in this tested setting.
